gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-carian: Commanding and a bit vintage, Woodgod leads. Noto Sans Carian keeps its terminals apart like open scissor blades, so Woodgod gets the swagger and the plain sans gets the quiet clarity.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-chakma: Approachable lowercase packed up toward the caps gives Noto Sans Chakma a friendly, compact look under Woodgod's vintage display voice. Their shapes sit together comfortably.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-cham: Woodgod's lowercase climbs nearly to the capitals, giving the heading a tall, vintage swagger. Noto Sans Cham, a modern sans with open c shapes, would drown that out if the heading were made small, so keep the heading big.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-cherokee: Noto Sans Cherokee forms a tall band of letters with short stalks above and an e with a wide gap at its terminal. Over many lines it moves along easily beneath Woodgod.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-chorasmi: Big x-height, short ascenders, and curves that stop short instead of closing in give this body a contemporary, open feel. Noto Sans Chorasmian then sits under Woodgod's commanding display letters like a plain sans taking over the talking.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-coptic: Vintage punch meets a tidy, modern texture. Woodgod is best at commanding attention with its wide-channelled bowls, while Noto Sans Coptic is best at settling into a steady middle-zone line with open s and c.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-cuneifor: Woodgod's lowercase rises nearly to the capitals, with a wide channel into every bowl, for a commanding vintage look. And Noto Sans Cuneiform does the opposite job, with an e that opens up and swollen, glassy lowercase forms that are best at plain reading.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-deseret: Woodgod's tall lowercase, which nearly touches its capitals, gives it a commanding, vintage stance at display size. Noto Sans Deseret is best at being plain and open.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-devanaga: Noto Sans Devanagari has a compact skyline where capitals blend into lowercase, plus a g with an open lower curve. But Woodgod's wide-channelled bowls and tall lowercase stand out above it, so the heading and body feel clearly separate.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-duployan: Wide-mouthed lowercase a and oversized e and a counters make this body feel contemporary and roomy on the line. Noto Sans Duployan would carry a long passage as a plain sans, comfortably and without fuss, below Woodgod's vintage heading.
